newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: News expected soon on S.Africa's AstraSat talks.
newsitem.headline: News expected soon on S.Africa's AstraSat talks.

text.p: An announcement could be made in the next two weeks on partners for AstraSat, the satellite television arm of South African public broadcaster SABC, a spokeswoman said on Friday.
"We should have an announcement late next week or the week after," she said.
AstraSat's search for partners to help it set up a six channel satellite network have taken longer than expected. The firm hopes to start broadcasting early next year.
Chief executive Gert Claassen said in August that news should come in October and Business Report newspaper said this week that an announcement would come on Friday.
The spokeswoman said talks were now in the final stages.
"Negotiations are still ongoing, but they are in the final stages on a number of potential local and international partners," she said.
The South African Broadcasting Corporation is to retain a 40 percent slice of AstraSat and offer international investors 20 percent and local players 40 percent.
AstraSat has a target of 125,000 subscribers a year after launch, rising to 600,000 in five years.

The launch of AstraSat is part of an expansion of the South Africa satellite broadcasting market, currently dominated by MultiChoice, that will also see the planned start-up of Christian-based broadcaster Uplink.
